text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Gangsters armed with a pistol, machetes and clubs raid the Stem Hotel in the town of Nakuru, robbing employees and visitors of an unknown amount of cash.
- The chairman of the opposition Raila Odinga FORD-Kenya faction says any alliance with FORD-Asili Chairman Kenneth Matiba must be genuine and sincere to win public support.
- Assistant Minister Andrew Ligale asks the church to play a conciliatory role in the debate on constitutional change.
- Radios and other high-tech communication equipment used by military and non-governmental organisations are stolen from a secure and tightly-guarded World Food Programme (WFP) store in Nairobi.
- Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae is accused of politicising the agricultural sector and turning a deaf ear to calls by coffee growers to implement full liberalisation.
- Outspoken Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) clergyman Timothy Njoya dismisses current opposition leaders as greedy people.
- Administration officials raid local brewing dens in the sprawling Mathare Valley slums in Nairobi, unearthing local brews buried underground.
- Rwanda has applied to the commission for East African Cooperation for membership in the regional grouping.

- Kenya lodges a claim with the United Nations for 1.14 billion shillings it says the world body owes it for its participation in various 1,000 dollar man-per month peacekeeping missions. The UN says it owes Kenya only 4.3 million dollars. ($1=56 Kenyan Shillings)
